findings.title: Degraded EXPLORE omits a trustworthy `next`
findings.recommendation: Fault-isolation clause (b) keeps 'any tuple fields that remain trustworthy' and omits `next` only 'when its source computation failed'. For an explore, the only throwing operation is the metadata read — `next`'s source (the newest valid emit's next_recommended, the record that already supplies the kept `last`, or the Early canonical constant) never fails. Reproduced: broken-metadata explore with a valid trail renders `last` but drops `next` in both tiers, text and JSON.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Align implementation: in the catch block, when ws.kind === 'explore', set next from the newest valid emit's next_recommended (or the Early canonical string when emit-less) — same trust basis as the kept last; render it in the degraded rows of both tiers.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Align spec before sync: amend the fault-isolation requirement so the degraded variant names the trail `last` as the sole surviving tuple field, deleting the 'when its source computation failed' conditional that currently promises next for explores.

findings.title: Degraded row is not a 'one-line error note'
findings.recommendation: Clause (b) specifies 'a DEGRADED row (name + a one-line error note)', but the row prints err.message verbatim — real YAML errors embed multi-line code frames, so the row spans 6 lines (reproduced in bare and --full). Collapse the TEXT render to the first line (error.split('\n')[0].trim()); keep the full string in the JSON error field.

findings.title: ⟲N-count spec text not updated for the adjudicated spine-valid content-based counting
findings.recommendation: The strip requirement still defines the count as '(review ⟲6 ✓ = six review-proposal-*.json emits)' — a FILENAME count — and the fault-isolation skip-effects list omits chip counts. The shipped behavior (deliberate, external system iter-1 resolution 3) counts spine-valid emits with command 'review' by mode; a spine-invalid review-proposal-*.json counts under the spec's letter but not in the implementation. This text syncs verbatim into the live baseline at archive. Before archive: amend the parenthetical to count spine-valid review emits of the mode, and add chip counts to the fault-isolation skip-effects list.

findings.title: Quiescent stages of MALFORMED docs never reach WAITING
findings.recommendation: deriveWaiting receives only program.parseable, but the bucket builder computes stage states for malformed docs' well-formed sibling stages and both surfaces RENDER them — a quiescent-awaiting-ratification sibling would show in the listing yet miss WAITING, while the spec's clause (a) predicate has no doc-class qualifier. Either pass parseable + malformed stages to clause (a), or qualify the spec text ('of a parseable doc') before sync.

findings.title: Workstream identity is name-only
findings.recommendation: A live change and a staging explore sharing a name collide wherever identity is compared by name alone (also-line exclusion, sprint-first sort). Key comparisons by kind + name, or document the invariant that propose's staging-move makes the collision unreachable.
